problems.problem_statement: A uniform chain, 10 meters long with a total mass of 20 kg, hangs vertically from the edge of a rooftop. How much work is done to pull the entire chain onto the roof? Assume the acceleration due to gravity is \(g = 9.8 \, \text{m/s}^2\).
problems.solution:
Let \(y\) be the distance from the rooftop, so \(y=0\) is the top of the chain and \(y=10\) is the bottom. The linear mass density of the chain is \(\lambda = \frac{20 \, \text{kg}}{10 \, \text{m}} = 2 \, \text{kg/m}\).
A small segment of the chain of length \(dy\) at position \(y\) has a mass \(dm = \lambda \, dy = 2 \, dy\).
The force required to lift this segment (its weight) is \(dF = g \, dm = 9.8 \cdot 2 \, dy = 19.6 \, dy\).
This segment must be lifted a distance of \(y\). The work done on this segment is \(dW = y \, dF = 19.6y \, dy\).
To find the total work, we integrate over the length of the chain:
\(W = \int_{0}^{10} 19.6y \, dy = 19.6 \left[ \frac{y^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{10}\)
\(W = 19.6 \left( \frac{10^2}{2} - \frac{0^2}{2} \right) = 19.6 \left( \frac{100}{2} \right) = 19.6(50) = 980 \, \text{J}\).

scaffolding.hint: The work done in lifting an object is the integral of force with respect to distance. For a hanging chain, different parts of the chain are lifted by different distances. Consider a small slice of the chain and determine the work needed to lift just that slice.

Define a coordinate system. Let \(y\) be the distance a segment of the chain is from the top of the roof. First, find the linear mass density (mass per unit length). Then, find the weight of a small segment of the chain of length \(dy\) at position \(y\).

The work \(dW\) to lift a small segment is its weight multiplied by the distance it is lifted. A segment at a distance \(y\) from the top must be lifted by a distance of \(y\). Express \(dW\) in terms of \(y\) and \(dy\).
To find the total work, set up and evaluate a definite integral by summing the work \(dW\) for all segments over the entire length of the chain. The chain extends from \(y=0\) to \(y=10\).
